speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. To understand what is causing this, have you noticed any fever, joint pain, or changes in your urine output recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pemphigus Vulgaris

The patient's history of mucosal pain (oral and genital) alongside cutaneous blisters, combined with the recent initiation of captopril, strongly suggests an autoimmune blistering disease triggered by a new medication. Before confirming this, I need to verify if the blisters are fragile and easily ruptured, and whether the patient has experienced any recent infections or stressors that could have exacerbated the condition.
